title: Hezbollah and Israel exchange fire over Shebaa Farms the day after the Hamas attack
body:
On 8 October 2023, the day after the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel, Hezbollah opened fire on Israeli positions in the Shebaa Farms, a roughly 39-square-kilometre area in southern Lebanon that Israel has held since 1967 and that Lebanon claims. In a statement, Hezbollah said it had fired guided rockets and artillery at three Israeli posts in the area "in solidarity with the Palestinian people."

The Israeli military said it fired artillery at the area of Lebanon from which cross-border mortar fire had come, and that one of its drones struck a Hezbollah post in the Har Dov area, which lies within the Shebaa Farms. Al Jazeera, citing Reuters, reported no casualties from this exchange. Lebanese authorities did not comment, and the United Nations peacekeeping mission in southern Lebanon (UNIFIL), which the day before had said it was boosting its presence in the south, had not responded to Reuters at the time of reporting. Hezbollah had also said on Saturday 7 October that it was in "direct contact" with the leaders of Palestinian armed groups.

The exchange marked the start of cross-border fire between Israel and Hezbollah that continued for more than a year, through the evacuation of communities on both sides of the border and the escalation of September 2024. It ended with the ceasefire that took effect on 27 November 2024, which Al Jazeera described as ending 14 months of fighting between Israel and Hezbollah.
